summary.headline: Om Power Transmission Q2 FY27 revenue rose 56% to INR 128.29 crore, EBITDA margin 15.25%, order book about INR 839 crore after October wins.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was INR 128.29 crore (+56% YoY) and H1 was INR 249.93 crore (+46%), with PAT of INR 13.85 crore for the quarter (+117% YoY). EBITDA margin of 15.25% was above the company's steady-state range, which management attributed to segment and project mix plus the specialised Dholera fast-track work. Order inflow picked up sharply after quarter end, with INR 273.21 crore of October wins taking the order book to about INR 839 crore before October execution. Receivables rose to INR 237.06 crore, largely retention from projects in advanced execution, while trade payables fell, driving negative operating cash flow of INR 38.20 crore for H1.

segments.name: Transmission line
segments.commentary: Management calls it the niche and highest-margin vertical; it made up 79% of H1 and Q2 FY27 revenue.

segments.name: Substation
segments.commentary: Contributed 17% of H1 and Q2 FY27 revenue; the 400 kV GIS substation at Dholera was commissioned and is described as a credential for future GIS orders.

segments.name: Underground cabling
segments.commentary: Share of the order book was low earlier; new orders from PGVCL (11 kV, Bhavnagar), two GETCO 66 kV orders, and UGVCL (Ambaji, October) have restored it as a meaningful part of the book. Margins are lower than EHV transmission lines.

segments.name: Operation and maintenance (O&M)
segments.commentary: Manpower-supply vertical fell to 3% of H1 revenue, which management linked to lower employee cost; O&M carries lower EBITDA margin and will be bid only where margins are acceptable.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at about 50% YoY; management reiterated this when asked about a higher run-rate path toward INR 720-730 crore.
Order book expected at INR 1,000-1,200 crore by fiscal year end, per Fenil Patel.
Long-term EBITDA margin band of about 12-13% and PAT margin of 8-9% on a yearly basis; management said 14-15% would be optimistic as a steady state, though a quarter can run higher on mix.
FY30 revenue target of about INR 2,500 crore, tied to entry into 765 kV tenders from GETCO and Power Grid and GIS substation orders.
Borrowing cost guided at 9-10% currently, expected to move toward about 8% as the CRISIL rating improves (cited as BBB+).
Dholera Package 2 to be completed by December 2026 and Package 3 by March 2027.
capex_capacity: Order book of about INR 839 crore after October 2026 wins of INR 273.21 crore, against INR 565.99 crore at 30 Sep 2026; about 1.9x FY26 revenue before October execution.
Projects are executed over 12 to 24 months; 765 kV projects are expected to take a minimum of 24 to 36 months.

Net IPO proceeds of INR 119.32 crore: INR 108.56 crore used by 30 Sep 2026 (INR 25 crore debt prepayment, INR 55 crore long-term working capital, INR 28.11 crore general corporate purposes, INR 0.46 crore capex); INR 10.75 crore balance earmarked for machinery capex.
Investment property rose from INR 3 crore to INR 5 crore; management said it is a rented commercial property added to build collateral for bank guarantees.
demand_pricing: GETCO tender flow was slow at the start of FY27 and picked up in September and October with a strong flow of awards.
Gujarat Wire-Free City Mission aims to convert overhead distribution networks in municipal areas to underground cabling by 2030, with an initial INR 500 crore provision for phase 1.
Bid pipeline of about INR 1,600 crore, which management expects to convert into orders in 3-4 months; it includes 765 kV bids for both Power Grid and GETCO.
Bids pending in Delhi and Madhya Pradesh, the first efforts outside Gujarat.
Management said competition has compressed O&M margins over time.

qa_highlights.question: Can margins of 14-15% be sustained in H2, and what drove Q2 margin uplift?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the annual EBITDA range is 12-13% and PAT 8-9%; the Q2 uplift came from transmission line mix (79%) and the specialised Dholera fast-track job, with quarterly results depending on project mix.

qa_highlights.question: Why have receivables risen to about 45% of revenue, and what is the collection plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Chetan Modi said receivables are high because most projects are in their last three to four billing stages, so retention (about 45% of receivables) has built up and is expected to normalise on project closure.

qa_highlights.question: Why is finance cost rising while borrowings fell?
qa_highlights.answer: Finance cost includes bank guarantee commission on the 10% performance guarantees required on GETCO contracts, which scale with top-line growth.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY30 vision and what revenue and margin targets are set?
qa_highlights.answer: Fenil Patel said FY30 revenue is targeted at about INR 2,500 crore, supported by 765 kV and GIS participation; management declined to give a margin target beyond the 12-13% band.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the INR 237 crore receivables is over six months old?
qa_highlights.answer: Chetan Modi said 84% of debtors fall in the under-6-months ageing bucket, which includes not-due retention as well as regular billing.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company be able to fully execute 765 kV orders alone?
qa_highlights.answer: Fenil Patel said Om Power would be individually qualified for upcoming GETCO 765 kV tenders without a JV.

risks_watch: Working capital: receivables at INR 237 crore (about 45% retention) and negative H1 operating cash flow of INR 38.20 crore; management guided to positive cash flow but gave no date.
Margin sustainability: Q2 EBITDA margin of 15.25% is above the 12-13% annual band management guided to, and the Q3 and Q4 mix is uncertain.
Order conversion: the INR 1,600 crore bid pipeline and the target of INR 1,000-1,200 crore order book depend on 765 kV and GIS wins that are not yet secured.
Concentration: order wins and execution remain largely with GETCO and Gujarat utilities; the first tender wins outside Gujarat are still pending.
Finance cost: rising bank guarantee commission on performance guarantees may keep finance cost elevated even as borrowing rates fall.
Dholera Package 2 and 3 completion (December 2026 and March 2027) and execution of the INR 621 crore unexecuted book, which management said would complete by June 2027.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and order momentum, with specific figures for October wins and the pipeline. More cautious and vague on margins, cash flow timing and FY30 numbers, where answers repeatedly fell back on project mix and stage of execution.
key_quotes: Underground cabling is now a meaningful part of our order book again, and with this mission under way, we expect the segment to be a steady contributor going forward.
A word on margins. EBITDA margin for the quarter was 15.2%, higher than our steady-state range.
As we have said before, individual quarters can show variance in either direction depending on which projects are at which stage of execution.

growth.why: Management reiterated ~50% FY27 revenue growth, backed by an order book of about INR 839 crore after October wins (INR 273.21 crore) and a INR 1,000-1,200 crore year-end order book target, plus a 1,600 crore bid pipeline; no new company-owned capacity or utilisation figures were given, so backing is partial.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guided a steady-state EBITDA band of about 12-13% and PAT of 8-9%, called 14-15% optimistic, and Q2's 15.25% was driven by 79% transmission-line mix and the one-off Dholera fast-track job, so margins should revert toward the band.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No new company-owned plant, line or capacity commissioning was discussed; the only mention is the 400 kV Dholera GIS substation already commissioned and capex of only INR 0.46 crore used so far.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 revenue growth guided at about 50% YoY (H1 +46% to INR 249.93 crore) and the order book of about INR 839 crore is 1.9x FY26 revenue before October execution, with a INR 1,000-1,200 crore year-end target.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No utilisation figure was given and no capacity expansion was announced; only INR 10.75 crore of IPO proceeds is earmarked for machinery, which is small, so a new capex announcement is not signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held the ~50% FY27 growth guide and reiterated it when asked about a higher run-rate toward INR 720-730 crore, and the bid pipeline of about INR 1,600 crore could convert in 3-4 months, but the upside depends on 765 kV and GIS wins not yet secured.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Receivables of INR 237.06 crore (about 45% retention), H1 operating cash flow of negative INR 38.20 crore, and Dholera Package 2 and 3 completion dates (December 2026, March 2027) create execution and cash risk to the 50% growth guide.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Entry into 765 kV tenders from GETCO and Power Grid (Om Power to bid individually, without a JV) and GIS substation orders underpin the INR 2,500 crore FY30 revenue target, but no dated launch was given and 765 kV projects take 24-36 months.

rows.label: October wins lift order book to about INR 839 crore
rows.why: INR 273.21 crore of October wins took the order book from INR 565.99 crore at 30 Sep 2026 to about INR 839 crore, about 1.9x FY26 revenue before October execution.

rows.label: Bid pipeline of about INR 1,600 crore to convert
rows.why: Management expects the INR 1,600 crore pipeline, including 765 kV bids from Power Grid and GETCO, to convert into orders in 3-4 months, but these wins are not yet secured.

rows.label: Positive operating cash flow, no date given
rows.why: H1 operating cash flow was negative INR 38.20 crore and receivables were INR 237.06 crore; management guided to positive cash flow without giving a timeline.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand, October order wins and the INR 1,600 crore pipeline, but cautious and vague on margin sustainability, receivables and cash-flow timing, and FY30 targets; analysts pushed on receivables, margin sustainability and whether 765 kV orders could be executed alone.
